notes_list.title: Resonance / Mesomeric Effect
notes_list.basic_overview: The Mesomeric / Resonance Effect involves permanent delocalization of π-electrons or lone pairs through conjugated p-orbitals. A resonance hybrid represents the true electron distribution and is thermodynamically more stable than any single canonical contributor.
notes_list.extra_info_content: +M/+R groups (+M: -OH, -OR, -NH2, -NR2, -SR, Halogens) donate electron density into a π-system via lone pairs; −M/−R groups (−M: -NO2, -CN, -CHO, -COR, -COOH, -SO3H) withdraw electron density by pulling π-electrons onto electronegative atoms. Resonance requires strict co-planarity of p-orbitals.
notes_list.examples: 1. Phenoxide ion resonance vs. alkoxide ion (phenoxide is ~10^6 times more acidic due to 5 canonical structures). 2. Aniline vs. Cyclohexylamine basicity (aniline lone pair delocalizes into aromatic π-system, reducing basicity). 3. Acetate ion delocalization (equivalent oxygen resonance forms).
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Requires parallel, continuous p-orbitals across 3 or more adjacent atoms. Steric Inhibition of Resonance (SIR) occurs when bulky ortho-substituents twist functional groups out of ring planarity, preventing mesomeric overlap. Solvent polarity stabilizes charged canonical forms.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Identify continuous p-orbital overlap (all sp2/sp hybridized centers). 2. Move ONLY π-electrons, non-bonding lone pairs, or radical unshared electrons (NEVER sigma bonds or nuclei positions). 3. Maintain net charge across all canonical forms. 4. Ensure second-row elements (C, N, O, F) NEVER exceed octets. 5. Rank contributor importance: Complete octets > Minimal formal charges > Negative charge on more electronegative atom > Maximum covalent bonds.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Resonance stabilization lowers the ground-state enthalpy (Resonance Energy). In electrophilic aromatic substitution, +M groups lower the activation energy barrier (Ea) by stabilizing the arenium ion (Wheland intermediate).
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Dictates ortho/para vs. meta directing power in aromatic substitution, relative acidity of carboxylic acids vs. alcohols, basicity of nitrogen bases, and regioselectivity of nucleophilic addition to α,β-unsaturated carbonyls.
notes_list.common_traps: 1. Never break a σ-bond or move atomic positions to draw resonance forms (that forms isomers/tautomers, not resonance structures). 2. Do not confuse resonance arrows (↔) with reaction/equilibrium arrows (⇌). 3. Halogens are −I > +M overall for reactivity, but ortho/para-directing due to +M transition state stabilization.
